sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,00,000/- from the respondent, on account of death of Elangovan Sengottuvel, who is husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioners No.2 and 3 and son of petitioner No.4, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 05-01-2024 at about 9.40 to 9.45 a.m., the deceased Elangovan Sengottuvel was riding Honda Activa Scooter bearing No.KA-05-JJ-9453 on Varthuru Main road,
near Spice Garden, Marathahalli, very carefully, cautiously, in a moderate speed, by wearing helmet and observing all the traffic rules.

At that time, one BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA- 01-F-9589, driven by its driver with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life, came from behind and immediate took right side, without showing any signal or indicator and dashed against the Honda Aactiva Scooter of the deceased.
Due to said impact, the deceased fell down on the road and the right side back wheel of the said bus ran over the deceased head and dragged few feet away from the accident spot.
The deceased sustained crush injury over his head and other parts of the body and blood bleeding from ear and nose and he has lost consciousness.
Immediately after the accident, the deceased was taken to Kaveri Hospital, wherein the doctors examined him and declared that he was brought dead to the hospital.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was working as an Engineer in Itron India Pvt. Ltd., and was earning a sum of Rs.2,51,335/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.

The Airport Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the Malathy Elangovan vs B.M.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129080501/
2 said BMTC Bus for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.5,00,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondent, the respondent has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement.
4. The respondent in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has denied the rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-F-9589.

It has contended that, on the date and time of the alleged accident, the bus in question was on its schedule trip from Kadugodi to Banashankari and the same was being driven by its driver slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.
While it was so proceeding, at that point of time one car was proceeding on the right side of the road, at a little bit distance.

The deceased came on a two-wheeler bearing No.KA-05-JJ-9453 from behind, riding the same in a rash and negligent manner, with terrific speed and in order to overtake the said bus and the car, sneaked between the bus and the car.

But, as there was no sufficient space between the bus and the car, due to over speed lost control over his two- wheeler and fell down on the road, at the right side back wheels of the bus and exposed himself for the alleged accident.
As such, for the alleged accident, the deceased himself was wholly and solely responsible and the driver of the bus in question was no way responsible.

However, the petitioners with the sole intention to make an unlawful gain from the respondent, have falsely implicated the bus in question and foisted a false case against the driver of said bus and in active collusion and connivance with the Police have got created false crime records.

The driver of the bus rushed to concerned Police Station immediately after the alleged accident and tried to lodge the complaint,
but the Police have refused to receive the complaint.
However, later the complaint was lodged before the higher Police authority.
He has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Elangovan Sengottuvel, succumbed to the injuries sustained in road traffic accident, alleged to have been occurred on 05-01-2024 at about 9.40 to 9.45 P.M., near Spice Garden, Varthuru main road,
Marathahalli, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-01-F- 9589?

sentences.text: Further, the petitioners have examined one more witness by name Jagathish K. S/o Kaliappan as P.W.2, who is said to be the eye-witness to the accident in question.
The P.W.2 has deposed in consonance with the evidence of P.W.1.

He has clearly deposed that, at the time of accident he was riding his motorbike on Varthur main road, from Kundalahalli Junction towards Marathahalli Bridge, near Spice Garden, at that time one BMTC bus was proceeding infront of his motorcycle in the same direction.
At the same time, the deceased Elangovan Sengottuvel was proceeding in his white colour Honda Activa bearing No.KA-05-JJ-9453.

At that time, the driver of the BMTC Volvo Bus drove the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and all of a sudden took the said vehicle to the right side, without showing any signal or indicator and dashed against the Honda Activa of the deceased.

As a result the deceased fell down along with vehicle and he was dragged few feet away from the accident spot and sustained severe injuries over his head, ear, left shoulder and blood bleeding from the nose and ear and other injuries all over the body and he lost consciousness.
Immediately the deceased was taken to Kaveri Hospital with the help of public by ambulance.
The doctor who has examined the deceased declares that he was brought dead.

12. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 12, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA- 01-F-9589, as well as negligent riding of the Honda Activa bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JJ-9453 by the deceased.
The said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding and sudden application of break of the scooter by the deceased.
Due to sudden application of break, the deceased has lost control over his vehicle and fell on the road.
At that time, the right back wheel of the BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-9589 ran over his head and shoulder and resulted in his death.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.12, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JJ- 9453 and due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-9589 and the deceased Elangovan Sengottuvel has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.

13. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of Honda Activa bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JJ-9453 and BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-9589 in the said accident, are not in dispute.

But, the respondent has specifically denied the above facts and circumstances of the accident as averred by the petitioners and has specifically denied the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-9589.

Further it has taken specific contentions that, at the time of accident, the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-9589 was driving his vehicle slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

At that time, towards its right side one car was proceeding and the deceased came riding his scooter bearing No.KA-05-JJ-9453 from behind, with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and in order to overtake the said bus and car,
sneaked in between both the vehicles, lost control over his scooter and fell down on the road, at the right side back wheels of the said bus and exposed himself for the alleged accident.
Further it is contended that, the deceased himself was wholly and solely responsible for the accident and the driver of said BMTC bus was no way responsible.
In order to establish the above contentions, the respondent has examined the driver of said BMTC Bus as R.W.1.

The R.W.1 has clearly deposed his evidence that, the accident in question has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the Malathy Elangovan vs B.M.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129080501/

At that time, towards its right side one car was proceeding.

The deceased came riding his scooter from behind with high speed and in order to overtake the said bus and car, sneaked in between both the vehicles, lost control over his scooter and fell down on the road, towards the right side back wheels of the said bus and exposed himself for the alleged accident.

In support of his oral evidence he has produced the reply letter issued by Police Inspector,
Airport Traffic Police Station, Bengaluru, one C.D., and copy of complaint submitted to the Joint Police Commissioner (Traffic), Benglauru, which are marked as Ex.R.1 to 3.
14.

On meticulously going through Ex.R.2 compact disc, it clearly reveals that, at the time of accident, the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-9589 was driving his vehicle with moderate speed, on the left side of the road and at that time, towards its right side one car was proceeding.

The deceased came riding his scooter from behind with high speed and in order to overtake the said bus and car, he rode his scooter in between both the vehicles, applied sudden break, lost control over his scooter and fell down on the road, towards the right side back wheels of the said bus.

15. The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent clearly establishes that,
the root cause of the accident was the rash and negligent riding of the deceased himself and not the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-9589.
The contents of Ex.R.2 compact disc is clear evident that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the scooter bearing No.KA-05-JJ- 9453 by the deceased.

The deceased came riding his scooter from behind with high speed and in order to overtake the said bus and car, he rode his scooter in between both the vehicles,
applied sudden break, lost control over his scooter and fell down on the road, towards the right side back wheels of the said bus.
Further it clearly reveals that, at the time of accident the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F- 9589 was driving his vehicle with moderate speed on the left side of the road.
This clearly goes to show that, the mode and manner of the accident as pleaded in the petition and deposed in the evidence of P.W1 & P.W.2 are completely false.

Further, as per the entire police documents produced by the petitioners themselves, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased/rider of Honda Activa bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JJ- 9453, as well as the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F- 9589.
In such circumstances, the petitioners cannot seek the Court to rely one part of the said documents and ignore the other part of the said documents.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Oriental Insurance Company Limited V/s Premlata Shukla, reported in (2007) 13 SCC 476, has clearly held that, "If a party produce a document and once the same is proved, he cannot seek to rely one part of the document and ignore the other parts of the document.

16. But, as per the Ex.P.12 charge-sheet, at the relevant point of time of the accident, the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-9589 was driving the same in rash and negligent manner.
Admittedly, the said charge-sheet has not been challenged either by owner or driver of the offending BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-9589.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the said charge-sheet/final report filed by the investigation officer, with regard to date, time and place of accident, involvement of the BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-9589 in the said accident and rash and Malathy Elangovan vs B.M.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129080501/

17. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on 30 feet wide on Marathahalli-Kundalahalli road, near Spice Garden, Varthuru main road, Marathahalli, Bengaluru, in between BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-01-F-9589 and Honda Activa scooter bearing No.KA-05-JJ-9453.
As per Ex.P.5 Motor Vehicle Accident report, the accident has not occurred due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident has not taken place due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of both the vehicles involved in the accident.

18. Further, the Ex.P.11 Post-mortem report clearly speaks that, the deceased Elangovan Sengottuvel has died due to shock and haemorrhage, as a result of multiple injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record, which goes to show that, the medical records produced by the petitioners are false documents.
In such circumstances, it can safely be held that, the deceased Elangovan Sengottuvel has succumbed to the grievous head injuries sustained in the said road traffic accident.

19. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, the deceased Elangovan Sengottuvel has succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident, taken place on 05-01-2024 at about 9.40 to 9.45 p.m., on Marathahalli- Kundalahalli road, near Spice Garden, Varthuru main road, Marathahalli, Bengaluru.
But, they have failed to prove that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA- 01-F-9589.
The oral and documentary evidence placed on record clearly establishes that, the root cause to the said accident was the deceased himself.
The said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased and skid and fall from his motorcycle.

But, as per the charge-sheet/final report submitted by the investigation officer and other investigation records placed on record, at the relevant point of time of accident even the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-9589 was driving his vehicle in rash and negligent manner.

As such, this Court is of the opinion that, the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-9589 has also contributed to some extent in the cause of accident and the death of deceased Elangovan Sengottuvel.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration that, the root cause for the said accident was the deceased himself, this Court is of the further opinion that, saddling contributory negligence to the extent of 75% on the part of the deceased/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-JJ-9453 and 25% on the part of the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-9589, would be justified and meet the ends of justice.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has already held that, the alleged accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-JJ-9453 by the deceased, as well as rash and negligent driving of the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-01-F-9589 and deceased Elangovan Sengottuvel has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.

Now the petitioners are required to establish that,
they are the legal representatives of the deceased.
In this regard, they have produced their respective Aadhar cards and Aadhar card of deceased Elangovan Sengottuvel which are marked as Ex.P.13 to 17.
The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children and the petitioner No.4 is the father of deceased Elangovan Sengottuvel.
On the other hand, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased Elangovan Sengottuvel is not specifically denied by the respondent.
Further, there is no contrary or rebuttal on record to disbelieve the above documents produced by the petitioners.
Therefore, it is held that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased Elangovan Sengottuvel.

23. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, " The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

sentences.text: According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
25. The compensation towards loss of dependency:

The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.

In order to calculate the loss of dependency, the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
i) Age and income of the deceased:
The petitioners have averred that, as on the date of accident the age of deceased was 48 years.

To substantiate the same, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card and driving licence of deceased Elangovan Sengottuvel, which are marked as Ex.P.17 and 19,
wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 01-05-1976.
Admittedly, the accident taken place on 05-01-2024.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased was about 48 years.

The petitioners have asserted that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was working as an Engineer in Itron India Pvt. Ltd., and was earning a sum of Rs.2,51,335/- per month.

Salary slips (total 5), Identity card, Form No.16 for the assessment year 2021-22 to 2024-25, Bank account statement, Income Tax returns for the year 2020-21 to 2023-24, Full and final settlement statement and leave details, which are marked as Ex.P.20 to 25 and 29 to 34.
